page: Amazon Web Services c6gd.8xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It is powered by custom AWS Graviton ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 processors, offering 32 dedicated physical cores and 32 vCPUs running at 2.5 GHz without simultaneous multithreading. Memory provisioning is configured at 64.0 GB of RAM, maintaining a compute-optimized 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio (2.0 GB per core). For high-throughput local I/O requirements, the instance includes 1900 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD storage alongside a 12 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. No dedicated GPUs are included in this configuration.

Benchmark results demonstrate consistent multi-threaded compute and caching capabilities, though single-core execution shows lower relative throughput. The 32 physical ARM cores achieve solid multi-core marks, including 48,571.1 on stress-ng multi-core and 11,706.0 on Geekbench multi-core, with capable clang software compilation (26,063.0) and ray tracing (27,349.0). However, single-core benchmarks trail comparable architectures, as reflected by a Geekbench single-core score of 958.0 and single-threaded gzip compression at 20.31 GB/sec. Memory read bandwidth reaches 1,894.03 GB/sec in small cached blocks and 173.34 GB/sec for uncached large blocks, though total memory score remains in the lower quartile.

The qualitative efficiency profile of the c6gd.8xlarge centers on dense physical core allocation and fast bundled NVMe scratch space. Because each vCPU corresponds to a full physical core rather than a virtual hyperthread, compute throughput remains predictable under concurrent load. The integrated 1900 GB NVMe SSD eliminates external network volume latency for high-frequency operations, making the server well-suited for distributed build pipelines, batch processing, static web serving (benchmarked at 33.11 GB/sec), caching tiers, and localized database workloads.
description: Amazon Web Services c6gd.8xlarge is a compute-optimized instance utilizing AWS Graviton Neoverse-N1 ARM64 processors with 32 dedicated physical cores and 32 vCPUs clocked at 2.5 GHz. It includes 64.0 GB of system memory, 1900 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD storage, and a 12 Gbps baseline network connection, with no discrete GPUs. Benchmark results highlight dependable multi-core scaling, such as 48,571.1 on multi-core stress-ng and 40.61 million operations per second on Redis SET tasks, counterbalanced by modest single-threaded performance. Because every vCPU is mapped directly to a dedicated hardware core, resource contention is minimized. The pairing of 32 physical ARM cores and low-latency NVMe local storage makes this instance effective for parallel compilation, batch data processing, static web serving, and distributed database workloads.
